newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean gold prices down, but demand slows.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean gold prices down, but demand slows.

text.p: South Korea's domestic precious metal prices have fallen this week in tandom with tumbling international prices and a continued influx of smuggled bullion, traders in Seoul said on Wednesday.

The daily selling price of domestic gold producer LG Metals Corp for the precious metal, which is regarded as a benchmark for the local bullion wholesale market, fell on Wednesday to 9,930 won per gram from 10,050 won a week ago.
The company's silver price fell to 148 won per gram from 152 won a week earlier.
Traders said domestic demand for the precious metal was unlikely to improve despite the weak gold prices in the world market.
A bullion dealer said one unusual development was a lack of North Korean gold being imported into the South Korean domestic market in June.
"We could not buy North Korean gold in June after one deal in May," the dealer said.

"As far as I know, there weren't any gold imports from North Korea in June. The North seemed to have put its bullion business on hold because of the three-year anniversary of the death of Kim Il-sung," the dealer added.

The telegraphic transfer selling rate for customers, posted by the Korea Exchange Bank, fell slightly on Wednesday to 891.60 won against the dollar from 891.20 won a week earlier. The rate is regarded as a benchmark of local foreign exchange rates for bullion companies.
